page.layout: One page of text in two parallel columns (left and right) above the main text block; running head at top; page number at top left. Left column runs first, then right column. Notes printed in the left and right margins are none. Text below the columns continues in full width.

main_text.p: in Paulo Samosateno, maximo licet Episcopo quod mundanas dignitates usurpaverit, & Ducenarius magis quā Episcopus vocari voluerit, quod per forum incedens numerosam catervam satellitum partim praecedentium, partim subsequentium, circa se habuerit, ita ut fides nostra, invidiae & odio propter fastū & superbiam cordis illius, facta est obnoxia. Eusebi li. 7 ca. 29. Vide Canonem Synodi Carthaginensis 4. Canonem hunc in corpus Decreti retulit Gratianus. Dist. 41. Can. Episcopus & Clerici. Episcopus (inquit) non longe ab Ecclesia hospitiolum, vilem suppellectilem & mensam ac pauperem victum habeat, & dignitatis suae authoritatem fide & meritis quaerat. Videatur Posidonius in vita magni Augustini Hipponensis Episcopi. Mensa (inquit) frugali usus est & parca, quae quidem inter olera & legumina, etiam carnes aliquando propter hospites vel quosque infirmiores continebat: cochlearibus tantum argenteis utens, caetera vasa quibus mensae inferebantur cibi, vel testacea vel lignea vel marmorea erant. Item. Testamentum nullum fecit, quia, unde faceret, Christi pauper non habebat: & de Basilio magno Caesarea Episcopo refert Sozomenus lib. 6. cap, 16. respondisse imperatoris
Collegium Iustitiae vel sessionem vocant: & in Camera rationum regiarum plures adoptantur. Quid memorem profusi luxus ostentationem in vestitu, famulitio & similibus.

page.notes: The two-column layout was read with the right column printed beside the left: the right column ("Collegium Iustitiae vel sessionem vocant...") is printed in the right-hand column and is transcribed as a foot paragraph at the top of the right column's continuation; the reading order follows the columns. The final line ("toris") continues at the foot of the page, so the paragraph is incomplete. Some words in the left column are in italic and have been marked. Doubtful: "Posidonius" in the italic reference line appears as "Pofsidonius" in print; "Eusebi" and "Videatur" readings marked for checking. Exact line breaks in the right column could not be fully verified.
